# arubasdwan_appliance_deployments (Data Source)

Fetches all appliances with their deployment configuration from the Aruba SD-WAN Orchestrator: hostname, serial number, and every configured IP interface (mgmt0/mgmt1, WAN, LAN, VLAN sub-interfaces, and loopback interfaces) including interface label, VRF segment, security zone, firewall mode, and bandwidth limits. For WAN interfaces behind NAT (typically carrying private addresses) the public IP discovered by the Orchestrator is included. Each appliance also reports its SD-WAN region, the applied template groups, the Business Intent Overlays (BIO) it is associated with, its locally configured static routes, the configured EC license, and the system bandwidth. LAN interfaces with DHCP server or relay enabled include the full DHCP configuration.

The data is combined from these Orchestrator endpoints:

- `GET /gms/rest/appliance` — appliance inventory (hostname, serial, model, site)
- `GET /gms/rest/deployment` — management and datapath interfaces, DHCP server/relay settings, EC license, and system bandwidth per appliance
- `GET /gms/rest/virtualif/loopback` — loopback interfaces per appliance
- `GET /gms/rest/tunnelsConfiguration/deployment` — discovered public IPs and effective shaping bandwidths of WAN interfaces
- `GET /gms/rest/vrf/config/segments` and `GET /gms/rest/zones/vrfSegmentZonesMap` — VRF segment and security zone names
- `GET /gms/rest/regions` and `GET /gms/rest/regions/appliances` — SD-WAN region definitions and assignments
- `GET /gms/rest/template/applianceAssociation` — applied template groups
- `GET /gms/rest/gms/overlays/association` and `GET /gms/rest/gms/overlays/config/regions` — Business Intent Overlay membership and names
- `GET /gms/rest/subnets/all` (fallback `GET /gms/rest/subnets`) — subnet table per appliance, filtered to locally configured (static) routes
- `GET /gms/rest/license/portal/appliance` — EC license assignments

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Read all appliances with their full deployment (interfaces + IPs)
data "arubasdwan_appliance_deployments" "all" {}

output "inventory" {
  value = {
    for a in data.arubasdwan_appliance_deployments.all.appliances :
    a.hostname => {
      serial  = a.serial
      region  = a.region_name
      license = a.license.tier
      # One entry per IP address: a dual-stack interface reports its name
      # once per address family, so group the CIDRs by name with "..."
      interfaces = { for i in a.interfaces : i.name => i.cidr... }
    }
  }
}

# Applied configuration per appliance: templates and overlays (BIO)
output "applied_config" {
  value = {
    for a in data.arubasdwan_appliance_deployments.all.appliances :
    a.hostname => {
      template_groups = a.template_groups
      overlays        = [for o in a.overlays : o.name]
    }
  }
}

# DHCP server/relay configuration of all LAN interfaces where enabled
output "dhcp" {
  value = {
    for a in data.arubasdwan_appliance_deployments.all.appliances :
    a.hostname => {
      for i in a.interfaces : i.name => i.dhcp_config
      if i.dhcp_config != null
    }
  }
}

# Read a single appliance by its Orchestrator primary key
data "arubasdwan_appliance_deployments" "branch01" {
  ne_pk = "3.NE"
}

# Server-side filtering: exclude virtual appliances and lab systems,
# restrict to two sites. Filtered appliances are never queried.
data "arubasdwan_appliance_deployments" "filtered" {
  exclude_models         = ["EC-V"]
  exclude_hostname_regex = "(?i)^(lab|test)-"
  sites                  = ["Berlin", "Hamburg"]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `cached` (Boolean) Whether to read deployment data from the Orchestrator database (true, default) or live from each appliance (false). Live reads are slower and fail for unreachable appliances.
- `exclude_hostname_regex` (String) Exclude appliances whose hostname matches this RE2 regular expression (e.g. "(?i)^(lab|test)-").
- `exclude_models` (List of String) Exclude appliances whose model is in this list (case-insensitive exact match, e.g. ["EC-V"]).
- `exclude_sites` (List of String) Exclude appliances whose site is in this list (case-insensitive exact match).
- `hostname_regex` (String) Only include appliances whose hostname matches this RE2 regular expression (e.g. "^br-" or "(?i)^(ber|ham)-").
- `models` (List of String) Only include appliances whose model is in this list (case-insensitive exact match, e.g. ["EC-S-B"]). Filters apply before any per-appliance data is fetched.
- `ne_pk` (String) Optional appliance primary key (e.g. "3.NE") to fetch a single appliance. If omitted, all appliances are returned.
- `sites` (List of String) Only include appliances whose site is in this list (case-insensitive exact match).

All filters are combined with AND and applied before any per-appliance data is fetched, so excluded appliances are never queried.

### Read-Only

- `appliances` (Attributes List) List of appliances with their deployment details, sorted by hostname. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--appliances))

<a id="nestedatt--appliances"></a>
### Nested Schema for `appliances`

Read-Only:

- `hostname` (String) Hostname of the appliance.
- `interfaces` (Attributes List) All configured IP addresses of the appliance, one entry per address: management interfaces first, then WAN/LAN (including VLAN sub-interfaces) in deployment order, then loopback interfaces. The interface name is NOT unique within this list — a dual-stack interface appears once per address family (IPv4 and IPv6). When building maps keyed by name, group with the HCL ellipsis operator (for i in interfaces : i.name => i.cidr...) or include the cidr in the key. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--appliances--interfaces))
- `license` (Attributes) EC license of the appliance: from the deployment configuration (sysConfig licence), filled in with the Orchestrator's portal license assignment for fields the deployment omits; all values empty/zero when no license information is available. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--appliances--license))
- `management_ip` (String) IP address the Orchestrator uses to manage the appliance.
- `mode` (String) Deployment mode of the appliance (e.g. "inline-router").
- `model` (String) Appliance model (e.g. "EC-S-B").
- `ne_pk` (String) Orchestrator primary key of the appliance (e.g. "3.NE").
- `network_role` (String) Network role as reported by the Orchestrator (e.g. "0" = spoke, "1" = hub).
- `overlays` (Attributes List) Business Intent Overlays (BIO) the appliance is associated with, sorted by overlay ID. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--appliances--overlays))
- `region_id` (Number) SD-WAN region ID the appliance belongs to (0 = Default region or regions not used).
- `region_name` (String) Resolved SD-WAN region name; empty if regions are not used or the name cannot be resolved.
- `serial` (String) Hardware serial number of the appliance.
- `site` (String) Site name the appliance is tagged with in the Orchestrator.
- `software_version` (String) ECOS software version running on the appliance.
- `static_routes` (Attributes List) Locally configured (static) routes of the appliance from its subnet table across all VRF segments, sorted by VRF segment and prefix. Learned and system-generated routes are excluded. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--appliances--static_routes))
- `system_bandwidth_inbound` (Number) System maximum inbound bandwidth in Kbps from the deployment (0 = not set; requires inbound shaping to be enabled).
- `system_bandwidth_outbound` (Number) System maximum outbound bandwidth in Kbps from the deployment (0 = not set).
- `template_groups` (List of String) Names of the template groups applied to the appliance, sorted alphabetically.

<a id="nestedatt--appliances--interfaces"></a>
### Nested Schema for `appliances.interfaces`

Read-Only:

- `behind_nat` (Boolean) True if the Orchestrator considers this WAN interface to be behind a NAT device.
- `cidr` (String) IP address in CIDR notation (e.g. "10.1.2.3/24").
- `dhcp` (Boolean) True if the interface obtains its address dynamically (DHCP/SLAAC). For DHCP WAN interfaces the current address seen by the Orchestrator is reported.
- `dhcp_config` (Attributes) DHCP server or relay configuration of the LAN interface; null when neither is enabled. The mode attribute selects which field group is populated. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--appliances--interfaces--dhcp_config))
- `firewall_mode` (String) Firewall mode of WAN interfaces: "allow-all", "hardened", "stateful", or "stateful-snat"; empty for non-WAN interfaces.
- `ip_address` (String) Configured IP address of the interface (without prefix length).
- `is_private` (Boolean) True if ip_address is private or otherwise not globally routable: RFC1918, carrier-grade NAT (RFC6598), link-local, and loopback for IPv4; unique local (RFC4193, ULA), link-local, and loopback for IPv6.
- `label` (String) Interface label name (e.g. "INET1", "MPLS"); empty if no label is assigned.
- `max_bandwidth_inbound` (Number) Maximum inbound (WAN to LAN) bandwidth of the interface in Kbps, from the per-interface shaper in the deployment or, when no shaper is configured there, from the Orchestrator's resolved interface view; 0 if not set (WAN interfaces only).
- `max_bandwidth_outbound` (Number) Maximum outbound (LAN to WAN) bandwidth of the interface in Kbps, from the per-interface shaper in the deployment or, when no shaper is configured there, from the Orchestrator's resolved interface view; 0 if not set (WAN interfaces only).
- `name` (String) Interface name (e.g. "mgmt0", "wan0", "wan0.100", "lan0", "loopback100").
- `next_hop` (String) Configured next hop / gateway IP address of the interface (WAN gateway for WAN interfaces, management gateway for mgmt interfaces). For DHCP WAN interfaces the current gateway seen by the Orchestrator is reported. Empty for loopback interfaces and when no next hop is configured.
- `next_hop_is_private` (Boolean) True if next_hop is private or otherwise not globally routable (same ranges as is_private); false when next_hop is empty.
- `prefix_length` (Number) Network mask as prefix length (e.g. 24).
- `public_ip` (String) Public IP address discovered by the Orchestrator for this WAN interface (the "discovered IP" of interfaces behind NAT); empty if none was resolved.
- `type` (String) Interface type: "mgmt", "wan", "lan", "loopback", or "other".
- `vlan` (String) VLAN ID for VLAN sub-interfaces; empty otherwise.
- `vrf_id` (Number) VRF segment ID the interface is assigned to (0 = Default). Always 0 for management interfaces; loopback interfaces report their segment on Orchestrator 9.7.0 and later (0 on older versions, which do not expose it).
- `vrf_name` (String) Resolved VRF segment name (e.g. "Default"); empty for management interfaces, for loopback interfaces on Orchestrator versions before 9.7.0, or if the name cannot be resolved.
- `zone_id` (Number) Security zone ID assigned to the interface (0 = no zone).
- `zone_name` (String) Resolved security zone name; empty if no zone is assigned or the name cannot be resolved.

<a id="nestedatt--appliances--interfaces--dhcp_config"></a>
### Nested Schema for `appliances.interfaces.dhcp_config`

Read-Only:

- `default_lease` (Number) Default lease time in seconds (server mode).
- `dhcp_servers` (List of String) Destination DHCP server IP addresses (relay mode).
- `dns_servers` (List of String) DNS server IP addresses handed out to clients (server mode).
- `failover` (Boolean) True if DHCP failover is enabled (server mode).
- `gateways` (List of String) Gateway IP addresses handed out to clients (server mode).
- `ip_end` (String) Last allocatable IP address (server mode).
- `ip_start` (String) First allocatable IP address (server mode).
- `max_lease` (Number) Maximum lease time in seconds (server mode).
- `mode` (String) Either "server" or "relay".
- `netbios_node_type` (String) NetBIOS node type: "B", "P", "M", or "H" (server mode).
- `netbios_servers` (List of String) NetBIOS name server IP addresses (server mode).
- `ntp_servers` (List of String) NTP server IP addresses handed out to clients (server mode).
- `option82` (Boolean) True if DHCP option 82 is enabled (relay mode).
- `option82_policy` (String) Option 82 policy: "append", "replace", "forward", or "discard" (relay mode).
- `options` (Map of String) Additional DHCP options keyed by option ID (server mode).
- `prefix` (String) DHCP subnet in CIDR notation (server mode).
- `ranges` (Attributes List) Additional IP allocation ranges (server mode): objects with `start` and `end` IP addresses.
- `reservations` (Attributes List) Static IP reservations, sorted by hostname (server mode): objects with `hostname`, `ip`, and `mac`.

<a id="nestedatt--appliances--license"></a>
### Nested Schema for `appliances.license`

Read-Only:

- `boost` (Boolean) True if the WAN optimization (Boost) add-on is enabled.
- `boost_bandwidth` (Number) Boost bandwidth as reported by the Orchestrator, passed through unchanged; 0 if not set.
- `tier` (String) Tier (throughput) license name; empty if none.
- `tier_bandwidth` (Number) Tier bandwidth as reported by the Orchestrator, passed through unchanged; 0 if not set.

<a id="nestedatt--appliances--overlays"></a>
### Nested Schema for `appliances.overlays`

Read-Only:

- `id` (String) Numeric overlay ID as reported by the Orchestrator (e.g. "1").
- `name` (String) Overlay name (e.g. "RealTime"); empty if it cannot be resolved.

<a id="nestedatt--appliances--static_routes"></a>
### Nested Schema for `appliances.static_routes`

Read-Only:

- `advertise` (Boolean) True if the route is advertised to SD-WAN peers.
- `interface` (String) Egress interface name; empty if not applicable.
- `metric` (Number) Route metric (lower value = higher priority).
- `next_hop` (String) Next hop IP address; empty if not applicable.
- `prefix` (String) Destination prefix in CIDR notation (e.g. "10.20.0.0/16").
- `vrf_id` (Number) VRF segment ID the route belongs to (0 = Default).
- `vrf_name` (String) Resolved VRF segment name; empty if it cannot be resolved.
